## Assertion 2 — The third preferred_label fix from proof_capture in one run routes to the non_converged terminal of the committed implement-work-item graph.

Proof mode: `factory_captured`

Reproduction steps:

1. Print `proof_capture`'s outgoing edges from the committed graph, and the engine build
   that will judge them:
   `git show HEAD:.claude-plugin/.fabro/workflows/implement-work-item/workflow.fabro | grep -n '^    proof_capture ->'`
   then `fabro --version`.
   Expect four edges — `needs_human` on `outcome=failed`, `fix` on
   `preferred_label=fix && context.internal.node_visit_count < 3`, `non_converged` on
   `preferred_label=fix && context.internal.node_visit_count >= 3`, and the
   unconditional `review` fallthrough — and `fabro 0.254.0`. Produces proof 03.
2. Hand the committed graph and two mutants of it to the engine. Write the script below
   to `"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/proof-capture/engine-leg.sh"` and run
   `bash "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/proof-capture/engine-leg.sh"` from the clone root. It copies
   the payload directory, strips the ONE fork-only `run.checkpoint.commit_timeout` key
   that the pinned upstream 0.254.0 release rejects (the same normalization
   `dev-tooling/checks/_fork_only_settings.py` performs — without it the release drops
   the whole settings file and renders every `inputs.*` default empty), and validates
   from inside each copy. Expect: the committed graph `Validation: OK` at exit 0;
   CONTROL A, which makes `proof_capture`'s only unconditional edge conditional,
   REJECTED at exit 1 naming `all_conditional_edges` on node `proof_capture`; CONTROL B,
   which replaces the literal bound `3` with an undeclared `inputs.*` token, REJECTED at
   exit 1 naming `condition_syntax` on edge `proof_capture -> fix`. Produces proof 04.

```text
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hands the COMMITTED implement-work-item graph, and two mutants of it, to the
# pinned engine. Run from the sandbox clone root.
set -u
SRC="$PWD/.claude-plugin/.fabro/workflows/implement-work-item"
W="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/proof-capture"

mkpayload() {
  rm -rf "$1"; mkdir -p "$1"; cp -R "$SRC/." "$1/"
  # The pinned UPSTREAM 0.254.0 release rejects the fork-only
  # run.checkpoint.commit_timeout key and then drops the whole settings file,
  # which would leave every inputs.* default empty. This is the same one-key
  # normalization dev-tooling/checks/_fork_only_settings.py performs.
  grep -v 'commit_timeout' "$SRC/workflow.toml" > "$1/workflow.toml"
}

# Run fabro validate in $1, record ITS OWN exit code, then show the matching lines.
validate() {  # $1 = payload dir, $2 = grep pattern
  ( cd "$1" && fabro validate workflow.fabro ) > "$1/validate.log" 2>&1
  local status=$?
  grep -E "$2" "$1/validate.log" || true
  echo "fabro validate exit=$status"
}

echo "### 1. the committed graph"
mkpayload "$W/committed"
validate "$W/committed" "Workflow:|Validation"

echo
echo "### 2. CONTROL A — proof_capture's ONE unconditional edge made conditional"
mkpayload "$W/mutant-a"
python3 - "$W/mutant-a/workflow.fabro" <<'PY'
import pathlib, sys
p = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); t = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = "    proof_capture -> review\n"
assert t.count(old) == 1, t.count(old)
p.write_text(t.replace(old, '    proof_capture -> review [condition="outcome=succeeded"]\n'), encoding="utf-8")
print("mutation applied: proof_capture -> review now carries a condition")
PY
validate "$W/mutant-a" "proof_capture|Validation failed"

echo
echo "### 3. CONTROL B — the literal bound 3 replaced by an undeclared inputs token"
mkpayload "$W/mutant-b"
python3 - "$W/mutant-b/workflow.fabro" <<'PY'
import pathlib, sys
p = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]); t = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
old = 'condition="preferred_label=fix && context.internal.node_visit_count < 3"'
new = 'condition="preferred_label=fix && context.internal.node_visit_count < {{ inputs.proof_capture_visit_cap }}"'
i = t.index("proof_capture -> fix")          # mutate ONLY proof_capture's, not proof_verify's
head, tail = t[:i], t[i:]
assert tail.count(old) >= 1
p.write_text(head + tail.replace(old, new, 1), encoding="utf-8")
print("mutation applied: proof_capture -> fix bound is now a template token")
PY
validate "$W/mutant-b" "proof_capture -> fix|Validation failed"
```

3. Decide which edge a `fix` verdict selects, per visit, from the committed text. Write
   the program below to `"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/proof-capture/routing-leg.py"` and run
   `uv run python "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/proof-capture/routing-leg.py"` from the clone root.
   Expect `visit 1 -> fix`, `visit 2 -> fix`, `visit 3 -> non_converged`,
   `visit 4 -> non_converged`; the two guards reported as exact complements; and the
   NEGATIVE CONTROL — the same evaluator over a deliberately gapped pair — reporting
   `GAP-OR-OVERLAP []` at visit 3. Produces proof 05.

```text
"""Which proof_capture edge a `fix` verdict selects, per visit, off the COMMITTED graph.

Reads the guards out of `git show HEAD:<graph>` (never the worktree), evaluates
them with the engine's own integer comparison over visit counts 1..4, and
requires exactly ONE conditional edge to match per visit. The NEGATIVE CONTROL
at the end feeds the same evaluator a deliberately gapped pair of guards and
requires it to report the gap — without that, "exactly one matched" could not
have come out any other way.
"""
import re, subprocess

GRAPH = ".claude-plugin/.fabro/workflows/implement-work-item/workflow.fabro"
text = subprocess.run(["git", "show", f"HEAD:{GRAPH}"], capture_output=True, text=True,
                      check=True).stdout

EDGE = re.compile(r'^\s*proof_capture\s*->\s*(?P<target>\w+)(?P<attrs>.*)$', re.M)
COND = re.compile(r'condition="(?P<c>[^"]*)"')
edges = [(m.group("target"), COND.search(m.group("attrs")).group("c")
          if COND.search(m.group("attrs")) else None)
         for m in EDGE.finditer(text) if "//" not in m.group(0).split("proof_capture")[0]]
print("committed proof_capture edges:")
for target, cond in edges:
    print(f"  -> {target:<14} condition={cond!r}")

guards = {t: c for t, c in edges if c is not None and "preferred_label=fix" in c}
assert set(guards) == {"fix", "non_converged"}, sorted(guards)
assert not any("inputs." in c for c in guards.values()), guards   # an un-expanded token never matches

VISIT = re.compile(r"context\.internal\.node_visit_count\s*(?P<op><|<=|>|>=)\s*(?P<n>\d+)")

def matches(cond, *, label, visit):
    if "preferred_label=fix" in cond and label != "fix":
        return False
    m = VISIT.search(cond)
    if m is None:
        return True
    n = int(m.group("n"))
    return {"<": visit < n, "<=": visit <= n, ">": visit > n, ">=": visit >= n}[m.group("op")]

def selected(guards, *, visit):
    hit = [t for t, c in guards.items() if matches(c, label="fix", visit=visit)]
    if len(hit) != 1:
        return f"GAP-OR-OVERLAP {sorted(hit)}"
    return hit[0]

print()
print("a `fix` verdict from proof_capture, per visit of that node:")
for visit in (1, 2, 3, 4):
    print(f"  visit {visit} -> {selected(guards, visit=visit)}")

print()
print("the two guards are exact complements:",
      guards["fix"].replace("< 3", ">= 3") == guards["non_converged"])

print()
print("NEGATIVE CONTROL — the same evaluator over a deliberately gapped pair")
gapped = {"fix": "preferred_label=fix && context.internal.node_visit_count < 3",
          "non_converged": "preferred_label=fix && context.internal.node_visit_count >= 4"}
for visit in (1, 2, 3, 4):
    print(f"  visit {visit} -> {selected(gapped, visit=visit)}")
```

5. Run the repository's own fail-closed graph gate, so the proof is not a one-off hand
   invocation:
   `LIVESPEC_FABRO_GRAPH_VALIDATION=fail_when_fabro_absent mise exec -- just check-fabro-graph-validity`
   Expect exit 0. Under that lever an unresolvable `fabro` is a FAILURE rather than a
   warn-and-pass, so exit 0 means the binary resolved, every committed payload graph was
   validated, and every graph's `all_conditional_edges` mutant was rejected as such — a
   mutant the engine failed to reject is a blocking finding in that gate, not a clean
   report. Produces proof 07.

What step 3 does and does not claim. It is condition ALGEBRA over the committed guards,
not an engine-executed route: this sandbox has no reachable Fabro server (see the
deviation note), so no run could be created to observe the routing decision. What steps
2 and 3 establish together is that the engine PARSES this exact expression — CONTROL B
rejects the identical condition with its bound removed, with a `condition_syntax` parse
error, so acceptance of the committed form is a real check of the grammar and not silent
tolerance — and that over visit counts the two guards are complementary and total for a
`fix` verdict, with the third visit selecting `non_converged`. The complement matters as
much as the bound: a gap between the two would drop a third `fix` verdict past both
conditions into the unconditional `review` fallthrough, reaching the reviewer with the
defect unreported.

Why CONTROL B is the load-bearing one. `constraints.md` forbids an `inputs.*` token in
these edge conditions, and the reason is exactly what the capture shows: the engine
expands graph templates at run-create time, so an unexpanded token leaves
`context.internal.node_visit_count < ` — a condition that does not parse at all. A bound
written that way would read as present in the file and bound nothing.

## Assertion 3 — The fix prompt directs the stage to read the latest proof record on the pull request when its preamble carries no finding, and to end through the structured needs-human ending rather than succeed on an unchanged tree.

Proof mode: `factory_captured`

Reproduction steps:

1. Print the two committed sections of the `fix` prompt, selected by heading:
   `git show HEAD:.claude-plugin/.fabro/workflows/implement-work-item/prompts/fix.md | awk '/^## When the preamble carries no finding/,/^## Your assignment/'`
   Expect the first section to name the second route (`gh pr list --head <publish
   branch> --state open --json number`, then the comments), to require the LATEST
   comment opening `Proof of Done — ` whose verdict is `not_captured` or
   `not_reproduced`, to state that an older `captured` or `verified` record is NOT a
   discharge, and to make "missing or unreadable" conditional on BOTH routes being
   empty. Expect the second section to permit exactly two endings — a committed tree
   change, or the structured needs-human ending — to state that it MUST NOT end
   succeeded with an unchanged tree, and to prescribe `git status --porcelain` plus a
   `git log` range before ending. Produces proof 08.
2. EXECUTE the route the prompt prescribes, against this run's real pull request. Write
   the script below to `"${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/proof-capture/fix-route-leg.sh"` and run
   `bash "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/proof-capture/fix-route-leg.sh"`. It needs `$GITHUB_TOKEN`,
   supplied by the run's credential projection; no credential value appears in its
   output. Expect the head-branch lookup to resolve this run's pull request number, the
   comment read to list every `Proof of Done` record on it, and `with_a_finding` to be
   `null`. Produces proof 09.

   The `null` is the point, and it is what a replay must read correctly. At capture time
   the pull request carried NO `Proof of Done` record at all, so `records` was `[]`. At
   replay time it carries at least THIS `captured` record, so `records` will be
   non-empty — and `with_a_finding` must still be `null`, because the prompt's selector
   admits only `not_captured` and `not_reproduced`. A `captured` record not qualifying
   is the prompt's "an older `captured` or `verified` record is NOT a discharge" clause
   holding, not a divergence from this capture.

```text
set -u
BRANCH="${LIVESPEC_PUBLISH_BRANCH:-feat/bd-ib-2s3kkq}"
echo "--- the prompt's FIRST prescribed command, run against this run's real pull request ---"
echo "\$ gh pr list --head \"$BRANCH\" --state open --json number"
```

```python
from __future__ import annotations

import re
import subprocess

GRAPH = ".claude-plugin/.fabro/workflows/implement-work-item/workflow.fabro"
EDGE = re.compile(
    r'^\s*proof_capture\s*->\s*(?P<target>\w+)\s*(?:\[(?P<attrs>.*)\])?\s*$'
)
CONDITION = re.compile(r'condition="(?P<condition>[^"]*)"')


def committed_edges() -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """`proof_capture`'s outgoing edges, in the committed file's own order."""
    text = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "show", f"HEAD:{GRAPH}"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True
    ).stdout

    for line in text.splitlines():
        match = EDGE.match(line)
        if match is None:
            continue
        attrs = match.group("attrs") or ""
        condition = CONDITION.search(attrs)
        edges.append((match.group("target"), condition.group("condition") if condition else None))

    """Evaluate one edge condition for a `fix` verdict at a given visit count.

    Only the three term shapes these edges actually use are understood, and an
    unrecognized term raises rather than defaulting to True or False — a silent
    default is how an evaluator starts agreeing with everything.

        if term == "preferred_label=fix":

            return False  # this leg evaluates a SUCCEEDED visit carrying a label

            raise AssertionError(f"unrecognized condition term: {term!r}")
        operator, literal = bound.group(1), int(bound.group(2))
        if operator == "<" and not visit < literal:
            return False
        if operator == ">=" and not visit >= literal:
            return False
    return True

    Returning a LIST rather than the first match is deliberate: a gap (nothing
    matches) and an overlap (two match) are both routing defects, and collapsing
    to a single answer would hide each of them.

    return [
        target
        for target, condition in edges
        if condition is not None and holds(condition=condition, visit=visit)
```
